newsitem.title: USA: Iowa bill to curb gaming withers as session ends.
newsitem.headline: Iowa bill to curb gaming withers as session ends.

text.p: Iowa legislators adjourned without approving a final version of a bill that would have set a three-year moratorium on issuing new gambling licenses in the state, an aide to the House speaker said Wednesday.
Their failure to act on the bill before the end of the session killed the proposal.

Both houses of the Iowa General Assembly had approved a three-year moratorium on new licenses, but could not resolve conflicts in other parts of their proposals, said John Davis, an administrative assistant to House Speaker Ron Corbett, a Cedar Rapids Republican.
The House late last week had approved the temporary halt, but also included a provision banning the use of credit cards at automated teller machines in casinos and racetracks.
The Senate, which also approved a three-year moratorium, did not give final approval to the credit card provision, Davis said.

Iowa Gov. Terry Branstad supported a five-year moratorium on new gaming licenses, but would have supported a shorter moratorium if a bill had been sent to him to sign, a spokesman said earlier this month.
